div.head: Abt 90
div.ab: Gif þeo steleþ, II gelde gebete.
Gif þeo steleþ, II gelde gebete.
Gif þeow steleþ, II gelde gebete.
Wenn ein Sklav stiehlt, büsse er [dem Bestohlenen das Entwendete] doppelt.
If a slave steals, let him compensate [the one robbed for what was taken] twofold.
If a slave steals, he shall pay twice the value [of the stolen goods], as compensation.
If a slave steals, he is to pay two-fold compensation.
If a slave steals, let him pay 2[-fold] as compensation.

note.seg: þeo, dahinter ƿ von anderer Hand
þeo, followed by ƿ in another hand
Hier darf nicht etwa, wie sonst oft nötig, als Subjekt ‘ein Gemeinfreier’ ergänzt werden, so dass þeo Objekt würde
Here, unlike in many other places where it is necessary, ‘a common freeman’ may not be supplied as the subject, which would make þeo the object
þeo ist älter als þeow früherer Texte
þeo is older than the þeow of earlier texts

[Ändere so die Notenzahl 4.] Die öffentliche Strafe, die den Freien träfe, fällt fort (anders bei handhaftem Diebstahl!), und die Busse ist geringer, als sie jenem zur Last fiele; o. 9; vgl. Gl Unfreie 17c. Der Herr, ist anzunehmen, diktiert ausserdem dem Diebe Prügel zu

[Change note number 4 accordingly (to ³).] The public penalty that would fall on a free man does not apply (unlike in the case of theft caught in the act!), and the compensation is smaller than a free man would have to bear; above 9; cf. Gl Unfreie 17c. It may be assumed that the lord in addition imposes a beating on the thief
note.note: Printed ⁴ in vol. I; Liebermann corrects it to ³ (III p. 17).
